items.title: Scott Robinson interviewed by Monk Rowe,Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997
items.q: to Anthony Braxton large orchestra, I played with the opera

ctx.x: Yeah. Well what I find is there’s incredible opportunities to play in an unbelievably wide variety of contexts. You know I do everything from the most classic jazz kind of thing — Marty Grosz and Peter Ecklund for example — to Anthony Braxton large orchestra, I played with the opera, I played with pop people, Elton John and people like that. In New © Hamilton Fillius Archive -4-

York particularly, it’s amazing how many different situations one finds himself in — film scores and whatnot. But what is lacking is the chance to actually have a group and play regularly, night after night with a group and develop a sound, develop a conception and a direction for your music. That’s what’s hard to do. It’s like you get plugged in here and plugged in there, and plugged in to all these different situations. But it’s really hard unless you either struggle quite a bit or unless you’re sort of one of…
